name: Oatmeal
lede: Oatmeal is a pale, warm grey-beige named for the food, and a color that old dictionaries and modern standards describe from opposite sides.

sections.title: The name
sections.body:
Paterson defines oatmeal as a greyish-yellow colour [1]. His colour tables file it among the yellows [1]. The name is that of the ground oat cereal, and our sources do not say when it became a color word; the earliest dated entry in the library is Ridgway's 1912 color atlas [2].

The library's standard, ISCC-NBS block 57, calls this swatch a "yellowish gray" [2]. So one source reads it as a grey-ish yellow and the other as a yellow-ish grey, which tells you how little separates the two: it is a quiet warm neutral, in the same family as [[beige]] and [[buff]] [2].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body:
In our archive of 23,781 paintings, 1,420 carry a color within six units of this swatch over at least five per cent of the canvas, as photographed [3]. That is more common than 90 per cent of the named colors [3]. Inside a painting it most often plays a light, in 53 per cent of the 1,031 paintings where we measured its rank [3].

The paintings where it covers most of the canvas include Ike Taiga's *Group Pilgrimage to the Jizo Nun* and Wu Bin's *The Five Hundred Arhats*, both works on paper or silk [3]. Much of this color is likely the tone of the aged support, not a paint [3].
